questions.q: What is a Step Functions state machine defined in?
options: JSON, using the Amazon States Language (ASL)
Python
A visual-only editor with no underlying text format
YAML using the CloudFormation template format
questions.explain: Step Functions state machines are defined as JSON documents written in the Amazon States Language.

questions.q: In a three-step Step Functions pipeline (validate, transform, load), what happens if the load step fails and has a Retry rule?
options: Step Functions retries just the load state, without redoing validation or transformation
The entire state machine restarts from the validate step
The state machine deletes itself
Retry rules only apply to the first state in a state machine
questions.explain: Per-state Retry rules mean a failure in one step doesn't force redoing work already completed successfully by earlier steps.

questions.q: What does a Catch rule in a Step Functions state do?
options: Routes execution to a different state (e.g. a failure-handling state) if the current state ultimately fails
Automatically fixes the error and continues as if nothing happened
Deletes the failed state from the state machine definition
Pauses the state machine indefinitely until manually resumed
questions.explain: Catch rules let you define what happens next when a state fails, such as routing to a dedicated failure/alert state.

questions.q: What problem does splitting a pipeline into a Step Functions state machine solve, compared to one giant Lambda function doing everything?
options: Each step stays small and independently retryable, instead of one monolithic function that's hard to test and retry piecemeal
It removes the need for IAM roles entirely
It makes every step run with unlimited execution time
It eliminates the need for any Lambda functions at all
questions.explain: Breaking a pipeline into states lets each step be focused, testable, and retried independently, rather than bundled into one hard-to-reason-about function.

questions.q: In the example state machine in this lesson, what does each state typically invoke?
options: Its own separate, focused Lambda function
The entire pipeline's single Lambda function repeatedly
A Redshift COPY command directly, with no Lambda involved
An EC2 instance
questions.explain: Each state (ValidateFile, TransformData, LoadToRedshift) is a Task pointing at its own dedicated Lambda function's ARN.
